# Brimholt repository instructions

- Brimholt is an original working name, not verified trademark/name clearance. Tibia is the design reference and its art style may be imitated closely: item, outfit, and monster concepts, silhouettes, colour schemes, and layouts. Names stay our own, never Tibia's exact names. Never copy Tibia's files (sprites, traced or recoloured art, maps, client data) or code: every pixel is drawn in this repository. **No recolour of existing icons**: every item icon is its own model or drawing, never an existing icon (ours or a pack's) in new colours.
- Use Godot 4.5+, typed GDScript, and native ENet/MultiplayerAPI. No Node server, third-party APIs, or paid services. Vendored code: LimboAI v1.6.0 (MIT GDExtension in `addons/limboai/`, keep its LICENSE.md) for bot AI behavior trees, and the training-only Godot side of Godot RL Agents (MIT GDScript in `addons/godot_rl_agents/`, keep its LICENSE; never shipped, no C#/ONNX) for training the PvP combat policy (`tools/training/`, `docs/bot-training.md`); run `make import` after a fresh clone so the extension is registered. The game itself never needs Python or .NET: trained policies are JSON weights run by `game/core/ai/policy_net.gd`. Downloaded assets must be CC0 (exceptions, the owner's decisions: the DejaVu Sans font under its free Bitstream Vera licence, 2026-10-17; the OpenTibia sprite pack, CC BY 4.0, 2026-10-21, used only as models for our own repainted variants with attribution, `assets/third_party/opentibia_sprite_pack/`), kept in `assets/third_party/` with their license file and a row in `assets/third_party/CREDITS.md`.
- Open Tibia engines are high-level references, not dependencies: do not copy/translate GPL code without a licensing decision; MIT reuse needs file/dependency checks and applicable notices. Neither source license licenses proprietary Tibia assets. See README.md.
- The world is `game/maps/overworld.tscn` (markers: Spawns/Ferrymen/Items and the rest) with its terrain in 128×128 sector scenes under `game/maps/sectors/`, painted in Godot's TileMap editor (terrain custom data). The overworld is 1920×1920 (`Atlas.OVERWORLD_SIZE`): the 384×384 heartland in its north-west corner, deep sea elsewhere until new regions are painted east and south; dungeons and caves lie in bands past its east edge. Generators load and save the map through `game/maps/map_io.gd`. Treat the scenes as the source of truth; do not regenerate it with `tools/generators/make_map.gd --force` without the user's approval.
- The game is a small LAN prototype for up to twenty-four players (Warrior, Hunter, Sorcerer, Druid classes, chosen permanently at trainers after the Adventurer's trial; clients never pick their own): original 32-pixel tile map, cardinal grid movement, collision, smooth presentation, host/join, visibly equipped items, a flat backpack with ground items and drag-and-drop, nine equipment slots, ten gear tiers (every five levels, accessories from 20, class weapons) and glowing level-50 relics from final-boss quests, a 384×384 overworld with instanced dungeons (`game/data/dungeons.gd`, `game/core/instances.gd`) (generated by `tools/generators/make_map.gd`) with a top-to-bottom coastal ferry, safe towns (zones flagged `town`) ringing a central lake whose island (Blackreed Isle) is a level 40-50 PvP hunting zone, coaches between towns for fast travel, the Hollow Reach endgame zone in the south-east (high-risk level 45-50 PvP where dying drops all gear but bound relics, obsidian Sanctum with the ultimate boss; painted by `tools/generators/endgame_zone.gd`), and level 1-50 balance curves anchored on a 700,000-health final boss that needs a twenty-player, all-class raid (`game/data/balance.gd`, `docs/balance.md`).
- Derive new mob, item, and progression numbers from `game/data/balance.gd` rather than inventing standalone values; regenerate `docs/balance.md` with `tools/generators/balance_table.gd` when constants change.
- Combat is Tibia-style and server-authoritative in `game/core/combat.gd` (target lock, 2 s auto-attacks, spells with own and group cooldowns, monster aggro, chase faster than players (no kiting), leash reset to full health on dragging too far or into a town, respawn, experience shared by damage or pooled in a party (`Combat.party_action`, shared-experience rules), per-monster loot tables in `Monsters.LOOT`, 10% death penalty with classic item loss, white/red skulls, PvP only in PvP zones and only between players who turned it on at Reedmere's warden (`Combat.set_pvp`; off by default, saved, 10-minute cooldown)). Derive monster and spell numbers from `game/data/balance.gd`; never trust clients with damage, health, or experience.
- Verify a feature once, at the end of the build, with the `feature-playtest` skill (lint and unit checks while building; visual, soak, LAN, and `python3 tools/testing/playtest.py --godot godot` only in the final pass, picked by what the feature touched). Read playtest findings, not just pass/fail.
- New or changed sprites follow the `art-direction` skill (palettes, outlines, light, sizes, and the look-once review). Qasrun (Sunreach) is the house style: new art must match its captures in `docs/art-reference/` and reuse its builders' patterns.
- New or changed item icons follow the `icon-art` skill (Tibia-style views, the builder to use, the volume and finishing passes, animation, and the side-by-side review).
- Bags hold items only in the three bag slots (`World.BAG_SLOTS`; their slots extend the backpack array); keep deeper nested containers, player-to-player trading, blessings, procedural caves, floor systems, world persistence (ground items, monsters), accounts beyond the identity token, and AI or dialogue-driven NPCs out unless the user selects them as a milestone. Characters persist only on the host (`game/persistence/`): never accept save data, positions, or stats from clients, keep saves signed and sanitized on load, and keep tests off the player's real saves (`--no-save`, `--fresh-identity`, `--save-dir`). Ferrymen, vendors, bankers, artisans, the PvP warden, and quest givers are static, menu-driven NPCs; vendor stock, prices, the bank, and the depot are server-validated (`game/core/economy.gd`, `World.move_item`).
- NPC interaction is a right-click context menu of services (Travel, Trade, Bank, Quests, Craft, PvP), never Tibia-style typed keywords. Add new services to that menu.
- Player input goes through `game/input/keybinds.gd`: never hard-code gameplay keys. New actions need a default binding there; the action bar has nine rebindable slots (default 1-9) that hold spells only (`"spell:<id>"` or empty); other actions get their own bindings in `Keybinds.DEFAULTS`.
- Peer 1 owns all gameplay state. Keep input ownership separate from node multiplayer authority. Validate RPC senders; clients request actions, never positions or authoritative appearance.
- Enforce movement timing, walkability, occupancy, item moves (reach, slot type, capacity, cooldown), and player limits on the server. Synchronize spawn, late-join, equipment, ground-item, and disconnect state reliably; send backpack contents only to their owner.
- Preserve host/client behavior parity. Art is original sprite sheets in `assets/sprites` (see `docs/art.md`): one layered sheet per worn item, never a sprite per combination, and never ripped or proprietary files: close imitations of Tibia designs are drawn here, not copied (CC0 effect textures live in `assets/third_party/`).
- Inspect actual files and reuse existing helpers before editing. Make surgical changes, keep types explicit, and surface errors.
- Consult the relevant repository skill before gameplay, networking, equipment, monster (`monster-authoring`), or validation work.
- Check tooling before claiming results. Use bounded checks, report what actually ran, and never bypass denied permissions.
- Keep registered checkout paths stable. Do not publish a repository, add a remote, or install system-wide tools without authorization.
- Layout and conventions are in `docs/architecture.md`: simulation in `game/core/`, catalogs in `game/data/`, drawing in `game/render/`, tests by kind under `tests/unit|integration|visual/`, generators and test runners under `tools/`. Use `make` targets (`make help`) for import, tests, and generators; update the relevant `docs/*.md` with each feature.
- Items live in `game/data/items.json` (shared with the sprite generator); stats derive from `game/data/items.gd`. Never hand-tune per-item stats unless the row sets `stats`. Relics are bound quest rewards (`Combat.claim_relic`), never loot.
- Rendering layers: the world draws in its own SubViewport with `lighting.gd` (day/night, zone ambient, point lights), `glow_layer.gd`, and `fx.gd`; anything that must stay readable (names, bars, numbers) goes in `world_overlay.gd`. Bosses use raid mechanics in `Combat._boss_tick` (enrage, pulses, wounds; Warriors swap with Challenge).
